OUTSIDE IMAGING CENTER - ULTRASOUND, ABDOMINAL AORTA (limited)
Indication: abdominal aortic aneurysm screening, 65-year-old man, former smoker.
Technique: Grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the abdominal aorta from the diaphragm to the bifurcation; diameters measured outer wall to outer wall.
Findings: Proximal, mid and distal abdominal aorta of normal caliber, each under 3 cm. No aneurysmal dilatation. Common iliac origins normal caliber. No periaortic fluid.
Allergies on requisition: penicillin.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.body: Texted a photo at 6:50 this morning: right foot red and puffy around the sore, worse since Sunday. Called him back. Says the foot feels warm and tight, the dressing has more drainage. Has not checked a temperature. With an ulcer that has been open since June, spreading redness needs IV antibiotics and imaging today. RIGHT FOOT, 3 VIEWS
Indication: diabetic with chronic plantar ulcer, new redness and swelling.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - Internal Medicine
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - INTERNAL MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959
Admitted 3/18/2025 via ED. Discharged 3/24/2025 to home.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (anaphylaxis); CEFAZOLIN (rash, pruritus - added this admission).

Reason for admission: chronic right plantar diabetic foot ulcer with new surrounding soft-tissue infection - erythema and warmth around the wound - requiring IV antibiotics and inpatient glucose management.

Hospital course:
1. Right plantar foot ulcer with soft-tissue infection. Foot films without osteomyelitis. Treated with IV vancomycin, levels followed with his kidney function. Erythema receded steadily. Changed to oral doxycycline for discharge.
2. Type 2 diabetes. Glipizide held; basal-bolus insulin with frequent fingersticks. A1c 8.2%. Fasting glucose 156, post-meal 198 on 3/20. After nocturnal low readings the insulin doses were reduced on 3/20.
3. Fever and drug reaction. Shortly after midnight on hospital day 3 (night of 3/20-3/21) he spiked to 38.4 C. The covering physician ordered a dose of IV cefazolin; within the hour he developed an itchy rash. Cefazolin was stopped; the rash and itching resolved over the following day without airway symptoms. Recorded as allergic reaction to cefazolin with penicillin cross-sensitivity. Fever did not recur.
4. Hypoglycemia. Morning fingerstick 48 mg/dL on 3/21, treated with oral glucose with prompt recovery; insulin reduced further. No further lows.
5. Hypertension. Metoprolol continued; BP 132/86 on arrival and controlled throughout. Lisinopril continued.
6. CKD 3b. Creatinine at his usual baseline during the stay.

Discharge medications: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 10 days (new); resume glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily. Insulin stopped at discharge.
Follow-up: PCP within one week; podiatry within 2-4 weeks. Continue offloading boot and daily dressings.

conditions.label: Allergic reaction to cefazolin due to penicillin cross-sensitivity

documents.title: Discharge summary review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospital summary reviewed. Cefazolin added to allergy list (rash/itching), penicillin anaphylaxis already listed. Doxycycline course noted. Post-discharge visit Friday 3/28.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 4 days after discharge from a 6-day stay for an infected right plantar ulcer.

He and his wife report he's doing well. On day 6 of 10 of doxycycline, taking it with food. Rash from the cefazolin gone within a day, no recurrence. Home sugars 120s-180s, no readings under 70 since he came home and no shaky spells. Back in the boot. Glipizide restarted at discharge.

Exam: afebrile, vitals charted. Rash: none visible. Right foot: plantar ulcer with clean base, the surrounding redness has faded to a faint pink rim, no warmth or drainage. Pulses palpable.

A/P
1. Right plantar diabetic ulcer, soft-tissue infection improving - finish doxycycline; podiatry next month.
2. Cefazolin reaction - resolved. Allergy list now reads penicillin (anaphylaxis) and cefazolin (rash, itching). Told him to mention both at every pharmacy and any hospital.
3. T2DM - back on glipizide 5; low in hospital was on insulin. BMP today.
4. HTN/CKD 3b - unchanged.
Call or text for fever or spreading redness.

documents.title: Weekend text - fever, flank pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Saturday-morning text, then phone. Three days of fevers and chills, pain in the right side of his back, burning when he urinates and going often. Feels washed out. With diabetes, CKD and his antibiotic allergies this needs blood work, urine culture and likely IV treatment - not a weekend phone prescription. Directed to the hospital ED now; wife driving. I phoned the ED charge nurse with his allergy list (penicillin anaphylaxis, cefazolin rash).

results.text: Escherichia coli, greater than 100,000 CFU/mL. Resistant to multiple antibiotics on the tested panel; susceptible to aminoglycosides (gentamicin, amikacin).

AREA HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN RECORD
Patient: Frederick Esposito, 65M  DOB 11/15/1959
Arrival 7/12/2025 07:45, sent in by his primary care physician.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), cefazolin (rash).
Home meds: glipizide 5 daily, metoprolol 50 BID, lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, ASA 81.
PMH: T2DM, CKD 3b, HTN, chronic R plantar diabetic ulcer (infected ulcer admission March).

HPI: 3 days of fever with rigors, right flank pain, dysuria and urinary frequency.

Triage: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 150/90, HR 98, RR 20.
Exam: uncomfortable, nontoxic. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. Lungs clear. Right foot dressing clean, ulcer without surrounding erythema.

Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 13.2. BUN 40, creatinine 2.2 (baseline 1.6). UA: pyuria, leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite positive.

ED course: urine culture sent before antibiotics. IV fluid bolus, then maintenance. Empiric IV aztreonam, selected because of his penicillin anaphylaxis and cefazolin reaction.

Impression: acute pyelonephritis; acute kidney injury on CKD 3b.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - pyelonephritis
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959. Admitted 7/12/2025 from the ED; discharged 7/20/2025 home.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis; cefazolin - rash.

Diagnoses: acute pyelonephritis, E. coli, multidrug resistant; acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3b.

Course: Started on IV fluids and empiric aztreonam in the ED. Renal ultrasound 7/13 showed no hydronephrosis. On 7/14 the urine culture grew E. coli resistant to several classes but sensitive to aminoglycosides. In light of his renal function and the susceptibility pattern, therapy changed to IV gentamicin with once-daily dosing adjusted for kidney function and trough levels monitored. Afebrile from 7/14; flank pain resolved. Seven days of active therapy completed in hospital - no oral antibiotic at discharge.
Creatinine 2.2 on arrival, 2.0 on 7/16, 1.9 on 7/20 (baseline 1.6). Lisinopril held during the admission, resumed at discharge.

Discharge medications: unchanged home list - glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with repeat BMP.

orders.reason: creatinine recheck after acute kidney injury

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after an 8-day admission for E. coli pyelonephritis (multidrug resistant, treated with IV gentamicin) with kidney injury.

Feels nearly back to normal; tired the first few days home. No fever since the 14th. No flank pain, burning or frequency. Eating and drinking well. Back on all home meds including lisinopril.

Exam: afebrile; vitals charted. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. Right foot ulcer unchanged, clean.

A/P
1. Pyelonephritis - clinically resolved.
2. AKI on CKD 3b - creatinine today; recheck in about 4 weeks to make sure it returns to baseline. Hydrate well in the heat.
3. T2DM/HTN - unchanged.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV, 65M.

The year: admitted in March (infected right plantar ulcer; cefazolin reaction; a low sugar on hospital insulin) and in July (resistant E. coli pyelonephritis with AKI, creatinine back to 1.7 in August). Since then he feels like himself. Still followed by podiatry; ulcer smaller in August.

Functional: independent with daily activities, drives, handles his own medications and his wife helps with dressings. No falls this year; uses the boot outdoors. Hearing adequate. Vision good, eye exam May without retinopathy. PHQ-2 0. Lives with his wife.

Meds: glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis); cefazolin (rash/itching).

Exam: vitals charted. Comfortable. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no CVA tenderness. Right sole: small clean ulcer, no surrounding redness; left foot intact. No edema.

Prevention: flu (high dose) and 2025-26 COVID given today. Shingrix, PCV20, RSV, Tdap done. Colonoscopy due 2028. Lung CT 9/23 negative; next fall. Aortic ultrasound normal in January.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin today. Diabetes, pressure and kidney medicines unchanged. Podiatry in November. Follow-up in 3 months for diabetes.
